requirements.verifier_assertion: report.total_files equals the number of files scanned
report.total_apparent equals the sum of all scanned files' st_size values
report.total_allocated >= report.total_apparent for non-sparse file sets
FileEntry.allocated_size == allocated_size_of(stat) == st_blocks * 512, falling back to st_size when no st_blocks
FileEntry.slack_bytes == max(0, allocated_size - apparent_size)
When allocated_size < apparent_size: is_sparse is True; slack_bytes is 0 (clamped)
parent UsageNode total_allocated == sum(children total_allocated) + parent direct_allocated (same for total_apparent)
hotspots sorted by total_allocated descending, stable secondary by path string ascending; root node excluded
breakdown_by_extension: row_for(key) by lowercase extension without dot; rows ordered by allocated descending; row has count and apparent
Files without extension go into one unified group in the extension breakdown
Breakdown.top(N) folds remaining rows into a '(other)' row; top(N).total_allocated == original.total_allocated
breakdown_by_top_directory(tree, depth=1) is available and uses allocated descending ordering
breakdown_by_age: every file lands in exactly one bucket; total_count equals total files; totals lose no files
Default age buckets include at least 'day' (files modified within 86400 seconds of ref_time) and 'older' (catch-all)
Custom age_buckets in config: [['label', seconds], ..., ['label', null]] — null marks catch-all; row order matches the custom labels
by-age Breakdown row order is age-bucket order (youngest first, oldest last) not by allocated size
CruftReport.category_totals() contains CATEGORY_EMPTY, CATEGORY_TEMP, CATEGORY_CACHE, CATEGORY_LOG, CATEGORY_BACKUP for the appropriate files
category_totals()[CATEGORY_X][1] (allocated) equals sum of .entry.allocated_size for all tags under that category
Files inside reference_roots are never classified as cruft when include_reference=False (the default)
Reference files are counted in total_apparent/total_allocated/total_files but FileEntry.is_reference is True
find_duplicate_sets reuses core.fs tiered hashing: bucket by size → partial digest → full/sampled digest
Files of different sizes are never in the same duplicate group (never read for hashing)
Files of same size but different content are not grouped as duplicates
Zero-byte files never count as duplicates (they are CATEGORY_EMPTY cruft)
DuplicateReport: group_count, duplicate_count, wasted_allocated, sets (list of DuplicateSet with count and wasted_apparent)
UsageTree.empty_dirs() returns UsageNode objects for directories whose entire subtree has no files
Files inside excluded_roots are not scanned and do not appear in report.entries
include_ext=[...] keeps only files with those extensions (case-insensitive, no leading dot)
report.entries are sorted ascending by path string; two analyses of the same tree produce identical ordering
analyze() makes no changes to the filesystem; file tree before and after analysis is identical
as_dict()['totals']['files'] == total_files; as_json() produces valid JSON with same ['totals']['files']; render_text() returns non-empty string
default_thresholds breach names correspond to limit keys: max_empty_files → 'empty-files', max_duplicate_fraction → 'duplicate-fraction'
ThresholdResult.passed is True when no WARNING-or-above breaches; INFO does not count as failure
SEVERITY_INFO < SEVERITY_WARNING < SEVERITY_CRITICAL; breaches sorted most-severe first; worst_severity is None when clean
merge_documents: list-type fields (roots, include_ext, etc.) are append-merged and deduplicated across documents
merge_documents: a key set to None means delete it; the merged result does not contain that key
load_session recognizes config keys: roots, include_ext, exclude_ext, detect_duplicates, age_buckets, thresholds
load_thresholds(settings) builds a ThresholdSet from the 'thresholds' block; returns None when block absent
analyze() raises InvalidScanRootError (subclass of DiskScanConfigError) for nonexistent scan roots, before any disk I/O
analyze() caches the result; force=True rescans; ref_time overrides the baseline clock for the analysis

All required symbols present at core.diskscan top level: ScanSpec, DiskScanSession, FileEntry, UsageTree, AnalysisReport, breakdown_by_extension, breakdown_by_age, CruftClassifier, find_duplicate_sets, load_session, merge_documents, allocated_size_of, and all constants
